primary_meaning: A wicked Gentile city that repents at God's warning and receives mercy, exemplifying repentance, divine compassion for the nations, and a model that will judge unrepentant hearers

alternatives.meaning: A proud, violent city destined for irreversible divine judgment and destruction
The oppressive Assyrian empire as historical enemy and instrument of chastisement against Israel/Judah

notes: Christian interpretation regularly draws on both the Jonah narrative (repentance and mercy) and the Nahum/Zephaniah oracles (judgment); the Jonah usage is the more frequent symbolic exemplar in teaching and preaching, yet the dual biblical portraits prevent a single settled consensus.
